verdicts.trueWording: AI reads us. Now it's time for us to read AI.
verdicts.note: Final line of the Guardian piece, byline 'Jeanette Winterson', dated 'Wed 12 Mar 2025'. Quote exact (curly apostrophe); closing-position and both limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: probably about 5% of the whole text is written directly from the generative AI
verdicts.note: Page: 'In her acceptance speech, Qudan stated: "This is a novel written by making full use of a generative AI like ChatGPT, and probably about 5% of the whole text is written directly from the generative AI."' Every limb (Akutagawa winner, acceptance speech, ~5%, directly from generative AI) supported; page hedges with 'probably'.

verdicts.trueWording: Hundreds of comments poured in on X, while the last announcement received merely dozens
verdicts.note: Page, paragraph beginning 'The internet had some thoughts.': 'Hundreds of comments poured in on social media platform X, while the last prize announcement received merely dozens.' Both limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: After a minimum 370 votes 3 of the 8 cases were undecided or incorrecly decided
verdicts.note: Main observations item iv, verbatim (page's own typo 'incorrecly'). 'At least 370 votes per poll' corroborated by item i ('minumum of 370 votes per poll') and the intro ('the polls with the least number of votes ... has 374'). Blindness of the test confirmed by the companion setup post ('The AI/human poll results will be revealed after the experiment concludes').

verdicts.trueWording: The 2nd and 3rd highest rated pieces were AI-written
verdicts.note: Item vi is verbatim and the conclusion repeats 'two of the top three rated pieces are AI written'; the results chart confirms pieces 2 and 3 (both red = AI) sit below only piece 4. But the cited results page never names a model: the string 'ChatGPT'/'GPT' does not occur anywhere on it. The limb is nonetheless TRUE and verified on the sibling post the page links as 'Read about the experiment here' (https://www.marklawrence.buzz/2023/09/so-is-ai-writing-any-good.html): 'some of the pieces were written by ChatGPT 4, which is the paid for version'. Fix by citing the setup post for the model.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: written by ChatGPT 4 - the cited results page attributes the pieces only to 'AI', naming no model

verdicts.trueWording: Below are (initially) 8 pieces of flash fiction, all of them ~350 words
verdicts.note: Setup post: 'Below are (initially) 8 pieces of flash fiction, all of them ~350 words. All of them were written to the prompt: "write a piece of fiction based on 'meeting a dragon"'. Two qualifiers the same page carries, neither contradicting the claim: 'for the AI there were additional very brief suggestions concerning tone &/or setting to generate variety', and 'the total number of pieces may exceed 8' (the run ended with 10; the results post analyses 'the first 8 pieces ... with the last 2 off to the side').

verdicts.trueWording: 8 - AI written (I asked for 19th century language, clearly unpopular choice!)
verdicts.note: List of pieces, item 8, verbatim. The 'low rating' limb is confirmed from the page's own results chart (results.jpg, read as an image): piece 8 sits alone at the bottom of the axis at 1.70 average rating, the lowest of all ten. Page's word for it is 'unpopular'.

verdicts.trueWording: the AI pieces all introduced the dragon in the opening statement, and did so in a similar manner
verdicts.note: Comment by Anonymous, 2 October 2023 at 08:37, verbatim in the served HTML (Blogger comments are inline, not iframed). Both limbs - every AI piece, and 'in a similar manner' - supported.

verdicts.trueWording: concerning that others were enticed by the AI's simplistic nonsense prose
verdicts.note: Same comment (Anonymous, 2 October 2023). Its subject is stated in the preceding sentences: 'Truly flabbergasted by the performance of #2. That is not a well written story.' Piece 2 is AI-written and the 2nd highest rated, so the 'highly-rated AI piece' limb holds.

verdicts.trueWording: The people voting on this included MANY writers, so we should expect better judgement from them
verdicts.note: Note i, above Main observations: '... so we should expect better judgement from them on writing matters than we would expect from the general readership or general public.' Both limbs supported; the note is a caveat Lawrence raises himself.

Paragraph beginning 'I had always avoided writing about my sister's death', exactly as cited: 'At first, in my reticence, I offered GPT-3 only one brief, somewhat rote sentence about it. The AI matched my canned language; cliches abounded. But as I tried to write more honestly, the AI seemed to be doing the same.' Live believermag.com returned a Cloudflare 403; verdict formed on the RAW Wayback capture web.archive.org/web/20220512115630id_/https://believermag.com/ghosts/ (full article body present), not on any summary.

verdicts.trueWording: In the nine stories below, I authored the sentences in bold and GPT-3 filled in the rest
verdicts.note: Final introductory paragraph before story 1, verbatim including the 'nine stories' limb. Raw Wayback capture (live site Cloudflare-blocked).

verdicts.trueWording: My and my editor's sole alterations ... adding paragraph breaks ... and shortening the length
verdicts.note: Same paragraph: 'My and my editor's sole alterations to the AI-generated text were adding paragraph breaks in some instances and shortening the length of a few of the stories'. 'Sole' supports the 'only alterations' limb. Raw Wayback capture.

verdicts.trueWording: I had never read such an accurate Modern Love in my life
verdicts.note: Parenthesis about the New York Times in the opening section. The passage praised is quoted on the page and is indeed built entirely of near-identical sentences: 'We went out for dinner. We went out for drinks. We went out for dinner again. We went out for drinks again. We went out for dinner and drinks again.' The claim's 'truest' renders the page's 'accurate' (the adjacent sentence does say GPT-3's language was 'almost truer than writing any human would produce'). Raw Wayback capture.

verdicts.trueWording: because it has not been edited beyond this, inconsistencies and untruths appear
verdicts.note: Final introductory paragraph before story 1, i.e. in advance of the stories, verbatim. Raw Wayback capture.
